chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal narrated from Abbas ibn Amir from Aban from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: A man came to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and said, 'I gifted a slave girl to the Ka'ba and was given five hundred dinars for her. What do you think?' He said, 'Sell her, then take her price and stand with it on this wall, the wall of Hira, then call out and give to every one who is stranded by it and every needy person among the pilgrims.'

key_terms.اَلْكَعْبَة: The Ka'ba, the sacred house in Mecca
key_terms.حَائِط اَلْحِجْر: The wall of Hira, a specific location near the Ka'ba
key_terms.خَمْسَمِائَةِ دِينَار: Five hundred dinars, a significant sum of gold currency
key_terms.مُنْقَطَع: One who is stranded or cut off from resources

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a slave gifted to the Ka'ba according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the nature of dedicating a slave to the Ka'ba by instructing the man to sell her and distribute the proceeds to stranded pilgrims (*muqattis*) near the Wall of Hira, rather than keeping her in service. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly view that 'dedication' (*taqarrub*) to the Ka'ba does not necessarily imply permanent retention but allows for liquidation to maximize charitable benefit, addressing the specific context of Hajj pilgrims in need.
